teams.synopsis: Multiple trades later, this still looks like the best team in the league — if Saquon's injury doesn't linger.
teams.blurb:
• Best RB duo in league
  • Lackluster WRs
  • Top 3 QB

Carmine has made multiple trades this year, and it looks like his team has improved because of it. Saquon and Pollard could win any matchup any week, and throwing Josh Allen into that mix can only help. He has the potential to drop 150+ any given week, but he'd better pray the Saquon injury doesn't linger, as his flex play without Saquon is debatably weak. Yet it still looks like the best team in the league, especially if Hockenson keeps playing at this level. Carmine is on pace for a record year, but he has a history of making some questionable midseason trades, so only time will tell.

teams.synopsis: Three great WRs, CMC, and the best D/ST in the league — Oh He Likes Cooking is primed for a great year.
teams.blurb:
• Stud WR group
  • Top 3 TE
  • Best D/ST in league

Ethan's team looks like the best team in the league — 3 above-average wide receivers with insane upside, paired with CMC, and his team may seem unbeatable. Not only did he trade his Browns RB1 for AJ Brown, he then picked up the new Browns RB1 on the waiver. Once he fills his RB2 spot, which will be soon, he's a lock for the playoffs barring any major injuries. Oh He Likes Cooking is primed for a great year.

teams.synopsis: Off to a strong 2-0 start — Tyreek and Kyren Williams could make this team's WRs the best in the league.
teams.blurb:
• Fixed hole at RB2
  • Kamara on bench
  • Questionable flex and TE

Nobody thought on draft day that Charlie would be here, but none of that matters, because he's here and it looks like he's here to stay. Tyreek Hill could drop 40 points at any given moment, and Kyren Williams has emerged as a stud. If Deebo keeps up what he did last game, this team could have the best wide receivers in the league. Gorman is off to a strong 2-0 start, and he hopes to keep it that way. Any given Sunday.

teams.synopsis: The best TE in the league and a 2-0 start — the RB2 spot is the last thing to fix.
teams.blurb:
• Best TE in the league
  • Above average flex
  • Questionable RB2

Quigley's team was questionable with the injury to Travis Kelce and Dobbins, but Kelce does Kelce things, and his first week back is another win for Quigs. Starting off 2-0 is always a good start, and Olave and Lockett have both been playing great. Meyers will be coming back and can hopefully take some stress off his WR2 position, but the real question is his RB2. How far can he make it without a starting RB, and will Jetty rear his ugly head and pull some strings to get Quigs an upgrade? Only time will tell, but until then, be wary.

teams.synopsis: No real weak spot on this roster — this may be Maney's year.
teams.blurb:
• Elite WRs and QB
  • Above average RBs
  • Consistent TE play

Cole's team does not have a weak spot in its roster; at a stretch, you can say Javonte isn't living up to his hype, but Derrick Henry helps cancel that out. Amon-Ra and Keenan are both looking set up for monster years if they can stay healthy, and Jordan Addison looks to be on his way to an OROY with how he's been playing. Not much else to say for his team besides watch out — this may be Maney's year.

teams.synopsis: A pair of fresh trades for CeeDee and Gibbs already has this roster looking sharper.
teams.blurb:
• Promising young RBs
  • Stud WR1
  • Uncertain tight end play

Max made some moves between last week and this week, bringing in CeeDee and Gibbs, and his team looks a lot better than it used to be. CeeDee Lamb looks like the guy in Dallas, and if the team keeps playing like they have, he has a chance to be the WR1 in fantasy. Gibbs is looking at a massive uptick in touches with Montgomery out, and even when Montgomery comes back it may be too late — it's Gibbs' season now. The rest of his team is solid; he just has to hope Waller can stay both healthy and consistent, as the Giants have looked touch-and-go this year.

teams.synopsis: Losing Aaron Jones stung, but Justin Jefferson is exactly who we thought he was.
teams.blurb:
• 2 great starting running backs
  • Stud first round pick
  • Questionable flex play

Ryan's team looks distraught after a week 2 loss — while he was missing Aaron Jones, it was still a morale dip to lose. Breece Hall looks to be a toss-up, at least until he's fully healthy, since the Jets won't play him if the game is out of reach, but the future looks bright. Justin Jefferson is the player we all knew he was going to be, and Tutu Atwell will be a solid WR2 until Kupp comes back. People forget who Ryan is — the man 'who can make everything out of nothing,' The Creator. He'll get you while you're not looking, so pay attention.

teams.synopsis: A season-ending loss at RB1, but Puka Nacua is quietly the next Cooper Kupp.
teams.blurb:
• Lost his first round pick
  • Promising WR group
  • Needs to find an RB

Andrew lost Chubb to a season-ending injury, and while an injury like that can usually ruin a season, Root still has some hope. Puka Nacua looks like the next Cooper Kupp, and as long as Kupp is out, Nacua is a top-3 WR any given week. Josh Jacobs needs to pick it up if there's any hope of Root making the playoffs barring a trade. Root is a slimy deal maker, and with any luck he'll turn this around — but if his team continues on this slippery slope, we may not be hearing from him much.

teams.synopsis: Not necessarily bad — Adams keeps this team in every game, but the recent trade is a gamble.
teams.blurb:
• Traded for Jerome Ford before knowing if Hunt would get signed
  • Uncertain flex play
  • Solid wide receivers

Deniz's team isn't necessarily bad — Davante Adams keeps him in any game, and Sanders and Cooper are both solid plays, but his most recent trade kind of throws a wrench in the gears: AJ Brown for Zay Flowers and Jerome Ford, who is not the lone Browns RB he'd hoped for. Deniz has to hope AJ Brown doesn't pick it up and Zay Flowers has an OROY campaign. A solid team with a competent manager is always something to fear — keep your eye out for Deniz to make the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: A very poor Week 2 without Ekeler — an easy matchup for whoever draws him next.
teams.blurb:
• Underperforming wide receivers
  • No clear RB1 without Ekeler
  • Lacking depth

Quin's team was ranked 5th last week, and he's subsequently taken a massive hit due to a very poor performance in week 2 — not even being able to manage 70 points is not a good sign for any team. His running backs put up under 10 combined and his WR1 had an off game, which raises real questions. A massive haul moved many of his original draft pieces; only time will tell if it was worth it. Without Ekeler, this team looks like a free win, so as long as he's hurt, expect Quin to be an easy matchup — but the seasoned manager always has a card up his sleeve, be ready.

teams.synopsis: An 0-2 start hides real talent — Brian Robinson looks like a stud already.
teams.blurb:
• Questions at running back
  • Inconsistent at tight end
  • Has to figure out what to do about Burrow

While I don't think Brandon's team is bad enough to be placed 11th, there is one thing that matters more in fantasy than a good team, and that is a good record. Brandon starting off 0-2 puts a damper on what looked like a promising year, but it's not over yet. Brian Robinson looks like a stud and his wide receivers are above average; Burrow and Pacheco both put a damper on this hype though, as they've both been underperforming. Brandon has a reputation to hold up, which I'll say he's earned, so don't be surprised if he shoots up the rankings in a week or two.

teams.synopsis: One piece — Cooper Kupp — away from being a contender.
teams.blurb:
• Solid running backs and flex
  • No real star without Kupp
  • Questions at QB

Ben's team is one piece away from being a contender, and that piece is Cooper Kupp. His injury is hurting Ben, as he doesn't have a true stud without him, which in a league as deep as this can greatly hinder one's chances at winning. Pickens looks primed for a breakout season, which could turn this team around — he just has to hope the Metcalf injury doesn't take a turn for the worse and he can play on Sunday. Ben's team may not look scary, but when it gets healthy, it can compete with anyone any given week.

teams.synopsis: Rose only because others fell apart — Chase looking lost is the real concern here.
teams.blurb:
• Questions about first round pick
  • Lackluster tight end
  • Very high ceiling but very low floor for this team

Baylen's advancement in the rankings is less about an improvement of his situation and more about the falling apart of others, as the spots 11-14 could all be argued. But what can't be argued is Jamarr Chase is looking terrible for fantasy this year, mostly due to Burrow underperforming, but until they figure it out, Baylen's looking at a rough time. Najee Harris is also getting phased out, but a good waiver-wire pickup in Zack Moss may help hinder the negative effects of that loss. Baylen is a competent manager, and despite an 0-2 start he is never truly out of the race — watch out for a blockbuster trade that will turn his season around.

teams.synopsis: Bijan is a bright spot, but Aiyuk's injury scare clouds the outlook heading into Week 3.
teams.blurb:
• Traded away starting QB in a questionable trade
  • Low-mid RB2
  • Flex remains a question mark

Anthony lost week 2 despite his team not performing terribly, but it did not improve from then on, and with Aiyuk dealing with a potential injury, his week 3 outlook isn't looking the best. Bijan has been an extremely bright spot on this team, but will he be able to do enough to bring Rolls with Butter into the promised land? I could see him skyrocketing in the rankings if he's able to win convincingly, although he's facing off against a tough opponent in Ethan Radecki.
